title: Supervised validation accuracy versus epoch
interpretation: Accuracy generally increases early, with model-specific later changes; the actual ViT-Tiny-dimension run is shown separately from the compact proxy.
limitations: Three seeds; standard deviation bars; the 12-block ViT-Tiny has notably variable terminal test results.

title: Training time versus epoch, raw and adjusted
interpretation: The ResNet epoch-2-to-3 interval dominates raw time; adjusted diagnostic removes 1,122.16 s from seed 11 after epoch 2.
limitations: Adjustment is analytical only, not a claim about true compute duration; no process logs identify the pause.

title: Marginal accuracy improvement per additional compute
interpretation: Marginal returns fluctuate and can be negative.
limitations: Per-second metric is sensitive to wall-clock noise; ResNet anomaly interval is excluded in adjusted calculation only if available in summary.

title: Dataset-size scaling for MLP and LeNet
interpretation: LeNet increases across the two reported sizes; MLP is not monotone across its available range.
limitations: Only 30K and 58K requested-size points; intervals with three seeds are imprecise.

title: Random Forest performance versus number of trees
interpretation: The curve provides a native model-size budget comparison.
limitations: Warm-start forest runs; no interpretation as neural epochs.

title: MiniBatch K-Means performance versus computational budget
interpretation: ARI changes over the algorithm-specific iterative budget.
limitations: K-Means reused-checkpoint duplicate rows are excluded; no epoch equivalence is implied.

title: Gaussian Mixture Model performance versus computational budget
interpretation: ARI changes over the algorithm-specific iterative budget.
limitations: K-Means reused-checkpoint duplicate rows are excluded; no epoch equivalence is implied.

title: DBSCAN performance versus dataset size
interpretation: The size sweep tests data-fit cost with fixed density settings.
limitations: Nine observations are parameter and budget conditions; no replicated seed error bars; mostly near-zero ARI per existing records.

title: Validation reconstruction MSE versus training budget
interpretation: Validation reconstruction MSE is reported separately for each representation model.
limitations: Three seeds; reconstruction and downstream metrics answer different questions.

title: Downstream linear-probe accuracy versus training budget
interpretation: Downstream linear-probe accuracy is reported separately for each representation model.
limitations: Three seeds; reconstruction and downstream metrics answer different questions.

title: Semi-supervised performance versus labeled fraction
interpretation: Algorithm and label-fraction effects are visible at the shared terminal budget.
limitations: Three seeds per condition; supervised baseline only where matched and present in raw result tables.

title: Semi-supervised performance versus training budget
interpretation: Methods have distinct trajectories at a common label fraction.
limitations: Three seeds; task adaptations, not canonical implementations on standard SSL benchmark splits.

title: CartPole-v1 reward versus steps and time
interpretation: Algorithm-specific return trajectories are shown for CartPole-v1.
limitations: Seed counts differ by algorithm; separate environments and reward scales; logged elapsed time is hardware/protocol specific.

title: Pendulum-v1 reward versus steps and time
interpretation: Algorithm-specific return trajectories are shown for Pendulum-v1.
limitations: Seed counts differ by algorithm; separate environments and reward scales; logged elapsed time is hardware/protocol specific.

title: Full WikiText-2 perplexity versus parameter count
interpretation: Larger checkpoints in the Pythia series have lower measured perplexity under the matched local evaluation protocol.
limitations: Six checkpoints across different model families; not matched pretraining compute, and tokenizer differences remain.

title: Pythia-70M checkpoint-prefix evaluation trajectory
interpretation: Loss is evaluated at released checkpoints, including step 0, on a fixed restricted local text prefix.
limitations: Single forward evaluations of selected released checkpoints on a small raw-text prefix; step-to-token mapping is published metadata, not measured local training compute.

title: Pythia-160M checkpoint-prefix evaluation trajectory
interpretation: Loss is evaluated at released checkpoints, including step 0, on a fixed restricted local text prefix.
limitations: Single forward evaluations of selected released checkpoints on a small raw-text prefix; step-to-token mapping is published metadata, not measured local training compute.

title: Zero-shot benchmark results (full validation splits)
interpretation: Three full validation tasks were evaluated without few-shot examples.
limitations: One model, three tasks; task scores are not pooled; smoke-test subsets are excluded.

title: Cross-paradigm within-task normalized changes
interpretation: Each panel normalizes a metric only within its own series; no pooled score or shared compute axis.
limitations: Index axis intentionally avoids pretending epochs, steps, and rewards are equivalent; percent change can be unstable near zero or for negative returns.

title: Supervised performance versus cumulative compute time
interpretation: Mean validation accuracy is plotted against mean cumulative wall time at each epoch.
limitations: Time is elapsed runtime, not energy/FLOPs; ResNet seed-11 pause-like interval is removed only in this adjusted diagnostic.

title: Semi-supervised method versus supervised baseline
interpretation: Pseudo-labeling is compared with the labeled-only MLP under matched fractions, seeds, and terminal epoch.
limitations: Three seeds per fraction; this ablation is separate from the 30-epoch Mean Teacher/FixMatch/MixMatch runs.

title: Representation quality versus reconstruction-model training cost
interpretation: Linear-probe accuracy is plotted against measured cumulative training time for each representation model.
limitations: Three seeds; the probe is a separate downstream assessment and does not represent a universal representation metric.

title: Perplexity versus comparable full-test evaluation time
interpretation: The same local device, precision, context, stride, and corpus protocol permit descriptive inference-time comparison.
limitations: Tokenizer-specific scored token counts differ; evaluation time is not original training compute and each model has one run.

title: Full-test evaluation loss versus parameter count
interpretation: Loss and parameter count are plotted for the same six local checkpoint evaluations.
limitations: Cross-family training data and tokenization differ; one evaluation per model; size is not training compute.

title: Restricted zero-shot benchmark smoke tests
interpretation: Three checkpoints were evaluated on 100 examples per task; this view is explicitly separate from the full Pythia-70M validation evaluation.
limitations: CPU FP32 smoke runs, limited examples; no claims about full-split comparative benchmark performance.
